items.s: From hoop stress = pd/2t, t = pd/(2 x stress) = 1.5 x 800/(2 x 140) = 4.29 mm.

A thin cylinder of internal diameter 800 mm and wall thickness 12 mm contains fluid at 0.8 N/mm2. Find the hoop stress in MPa.
items.s: Hoop stress = p d/(2t) = 0.8 x 800/(2 x 12) = 26.67 MPa.

items.q: A closed thin cylinder of diameter 900 mm, wall thickness 12 mm carries internal pressure 1.5 N/mm2. Find the longitudinal stress in MPa.
items.s: Longitudinal stress = p d/(4t) = 1.5 x 900/(4 x 12) = 28.12 MPa, half the hoop stress.

items.q: What wall thickness, in mm, is required for a thin cylinder of diameter 800 mm to carry 2.5 N/mm2 if the hoop stress must not exceed 80 MPa?
items.s: From hoop stress = pd/2t, t = pd/(2 x stress) = 2.5 x 800/(2 x 80) = 12.5 mm.

items.q: A thin spherical shell of internal diameter 1000 mm and thickness 12 mm contains gas at 1.2 N/mm2. Find the tensile stress in the shell in MPa.
items.s: Stress = p d/(4t) = 1.2 x 1000/(4 x 12) = 25 MPa, the same in every direction.

items.q: A spherical tank of diameter 900 mm must not exceed 60 MPa at an internal pressure of 1.0 N/mm2. Find the required thickness in mm.

A member of volume 500000 mm3 is stressed uniformly to 80 MPa. With E = 210 GPa, find the strain energy stored, in J.
A column fixed at the base and free at the top is 2 m high with EI = 200 GPa x 3 x 10^6 mm4. Find the buckling load in kN.
items.s: Effective length is 2L, so P = pi^2 EI/(2L)^2 = 370.1 kN.
